newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot prod diffs little changed despite rumors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot prod diffs little changed despite rumors.

text.p: Activity in the spot products market remained choppy early Thursday as traders sought to pin down diffs in New York Harbor following the roll in the spot futures.
A spate of rumors regarding possible refinery outages on the U.S. Gulf also emerged, traders said, increasing market anxieties.

Most of the refinery questions concerned Corpus Christi facilities. Citgo is expected to restart a 65,000 barrel per day cracker this weekend at its refinery there, while some talk emerged about problems at Valero's refinery.
In addition, speculation that Coastal may be suffering a problem at its Corpus Christi refinery emerged late Wednesday after the company was seen reselling crude oil.
Traders said that although most of the talk did not appear to be true, there was probably some basis for the speculation.
"We've seen some ongoing issues around Corpus," one trader said. "And where there's smoke there's usually fire."
Some concerns that Amerada Hess's St. Croix refinery would bring down a reformer in May for five weeks also circulated in the market.
NYH prompt No. 2 oil diffs were put between about 3.50 and 3.75 cents over the screen, while prompt low sulphur was seen between 4.50 and 4.75 cents over the screen.
In the USG, low sulphur diesel for 13th cycle delivery on the Colonial Pipeline was talked at 0.50 cents under the screen, down about 0.20 cent from late Wednesday levels.
On the NYMEX, the June products were firmer at midday after the expiration of the May futures at the close of trading Wednesday.
